# Results — Study 450 (Andrews' Pitchfork)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **price
respects the fork: a touch of the lower tine bounces back toward the median line** — encoded as
a mechanical rule. Pivots are confirmed fractals (k = 10, with a 10-bar confirmation lag); at
every bar the fork is anchored on the three latest confirmed pivots; a long fires on the first
close below the lower tine, entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure
the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **819** mechanical lower-tine touches pooled across the 5 tapes (k = 10) |
| Timing / costs | confirmed-fractal pivots usable only **+10 bars** later; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per touch |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument trend study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — lower-tine touch vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch touch-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = touch − random.

| horizon | n | touch | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (touch−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 819 | +39.0 bps | 61% | +3.81 | +48.5 bps | **−9.5 bps** | +37.0 bps | −0.73 | 0.467 |
| 10-day | 818 | +40.1 bps | 60% | +2.63 | +65.6 bps | **−25.5 bps** | +38.1 bps | −1.44 | 0.150 |
| 20-day | 818 | +92.2 bps | 62% | +3.93 | +131.3 bps | **−39.1 bps** | +90.2 bps | −1.61 | 0.107 |
| 60-day | 811 | +305.0 bps | 70% | +6.47 | +232.1 bps | **+72.8 bps** | +303.0 bps | +1.77 | 0.078 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+3.93** at 20 days,
**+6.47** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the lower-tine touch is
*worse* at 5/10/20 days (Δ = −9.5 / −25.5 / −39.1 bps) and only nominally better at 60 days
(+72.8 bps). The touch-minus-random difference **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (max
Welch *t* = +1.77 at 60 days, *p* = 0.078). The fork does not forecast.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the touch loses to random almost everywhere

| ticker | entries | touch | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (touch−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 161 | +51.7 bps | +0.92 | +132.9 bps | **−81.2 bps** |
| QQQ | 162 | +134.7 bps | +2.59 | +182.2 bps | **−47.5 bps** |
| IWM | 159 | +75.3 bps | +1.27 | +107.4 bps | **−32.1 bps** |
| DIA | 144 | +110.0 bps | +2.26 | +92.8 bps | **+17.3 bps** |
| GLD | 193 | +91.0 bps | +2.12 | +135.8 bps | **−44.9 bps** |

Only **DIA** edges out a positive delta (+17.3 bps); in 4 of 5 names the famous fork
*underperforms* a dart-throwing entry. No coherent cross-sectional edge — the hallmark of
relabelled drift.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the fork, nothing changes

The decisive "does the geometry matter?" test: keep the pivot **positions** and the price
**marginal**, but permute which price sits at which pivot, so the fork lines become geometric
nonsense. If price genuinely respected *these specific lines*, the scramble would collapse the
result.

| test | observed lower-tine 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-pivot fork | +51.7 bps | **0.611** | 500 |

**61% of scrambled-geometry forks match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.611). The Andrews lines
carry no information — geometric nonsense does just as well. "Price respects the fork" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real bounce

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* tine-bounce (knob `edge`), the same lower-tine rule
behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a
dead detector.

| planted edge | n | touch | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no bounce) | 111 | −21.0 bps | 48% | −0.52 |
| **0.40** (real planted bounce) | 122 | +110.9 bps | 64% | **+3.44** |

With no planted bounce the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted bounce
lights up at *t* = +3.44 with a 64% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The lower-tine touch does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (touch − random = −9.5 / −25.5 / −39.1 / +72.8 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the touch-vs-random
  Welch *t* never clears 2, max +1.77 at 60 days, *p* = 0.078). The impressive one-sample
  *t*'s (20-day +3.93, 60-day +6.47) are pure beta — the upward drift of long equity indices.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and costs only deepen the hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply and more
  fully by holding the index; the fork rule trades less and pays costs on each touch, dominating
  nothing. No capacity question because there is no edge to scale.
- **"Price respects the fork"? — BUSTED.** The shuffled-pivot placebo leaves the result intact
  (*p* = 0.611): geometric-nonsense forks do as well as the real ones, so the specific Andrews
  median line and tines carry no forecasting information. The pitchfork is a descriptive drawing
  tool, not a forecasting strategy.
